title: Meadows, Shepherd Huts, and Silence
lead: A park in the heart of the Gorce Mountains. Clearings, wooden shepherd huts, fir forests, and the most beautiful views of the Tatras and Beskids.
body:
A Park in the Heart of the Gorce

Gorce National Park covers the central part of the Gorce — a mountain range lying between the Tatras and the Beskid Wyspowy. It is a park that protects the unique landscape of mountain meadows and clearings, covered with tall grasses and herbs, and extensive fir-beech forests that once covered the entire Carpathians.

The symbol of the park is Turbacz (1,310 m) — the highest peak of the Gorce, on which a mountain hut is located. From Turbacz, one of the most beautiful views in Poland opens up — with good weather you can see the Tatras, Pieniny, Beskid Sądecki, and Żywiec Beskids.

Meadows, Shepherd Huts, and Pastoral Tradition

The Gorce is a land of pastoral tradition that has survived here to this day. Sheep still graze on the mountain meadows, and in wooden shepherd huts you can meet shepherds making oscypek and bundz — traditional sheep cheeses. This is a living open-air museum of pastoral culture worth getting to know.

The park offers many trails — from easy walks to demanding hikes. The most popular routes lead to Turbacz, Hala Długa, and Stare Wierchy. It is worth planning the trip to see as much as possible — the Gorce are beautiful in every season.
tip: Stop at the Turbacz mountain hut — one of the oldest in Poland. In the evening, you can listen to highland music around the campfire.
